samples.text: Floating-point addition is not associative because rounding errors introduced during each operation can vary depending on the order of computation. For example, (a + b) + c may yield a different result than a + (b + c) due to intermediate rounding. This occurs because floating-point numbers have limited precision, so the order in which additions are performed affects which bits are lost during rounding.

For example, (a + b) + c may yield a different value than a + (b + c) when the intermediate sums exceed the precision limits of the floating-point format.
